FILED s465 (Fable, 2026-09-02) from the USER decision on docs/plan-test-audit-s464.md Â§5.5 ("Ratify as standing").

THE RULE: a ruled refusal (docs/not-supported.md entry + perl-shaped message) is a STATEMENT-level event: the refused statement lowers to a trappable run-time die at its site -- the same shape as the drop form (ir-spec Â§9.3) and the announce->DIE flip (plan-post-s433) -- and the REST of the file runs.  A refusal that aborts the whole transpile ("TRANSPILE_FAIL") is a bug in the refusal, not a property of the feature.

FIRST INSTANCE: perl-tests/state.t -- `PCL: given/when (feature 'switch') is not supported -- removed in perl 5.42, at state.t line N` kills the file; it had 157 passing rows at s414 (sweep TOTAL lost them at s415, recorded then as "one given block").  After the conversion the `given` statement dies when REACHED (perl-shaped text, trappable in eval, `$@` carries it), the file's other rows run, and state.t's rows enter baselines/pass-baseline.tsv / fail-baseline.tsv by EDIT with causes.  Then #965's 46 state.t inline `ok(1, 'SKIP')` rows can be restored (FIX or registry).

THEN: grep Pl/ for every other refusal that dies at TRANSPILE time with a "not supported" text (the ruled list lives in not-supported.md; the compiler sites are the `die "PCL: ..."` calls in Pl/Parser2.pm / Pl/Parser.pm / Pl/PExpr.pm) and classify each: (a) statement-shaped (a compound statement or a statement-level construct) -> convert to the site-die; (b) EXPRESSION-shaped inside a larger statement -> the enclosing statement is the unit (the drop form's unit); (c) FILE-shaped for a real reason (e.g. a source filter, a `BEGIN` that changes the parse of everything after it) -> stays file-level, with the reason written into the not-supported entry.  One guard row per converted refusal (the file runs to its end; the refused statement dies with the ruled text; a row AFTER it passes).

BARS: gate; corpus-diff (the refusal sites move) with every diff explained; the full sweep with state.t's rows blessed by edit (TOTAL should rise by ~157); the census (a converted refusal is NOT a drop -- keep the drop census at 5); companion `--quick` if any t/ file carried the same refusal (grep the snapshot notes for "not supported").
RELATED: #965, #993, plan-post-s433 (the flip), ir-spec Â§9.3, DECIDED Â§s465.
